# Cross-run reuse examples

Use this when `project.md` already lists shared components. Match the incoming region to the inventory by rendered shape, interaction, and screenshot—not by identical source.

## One incoming occurrence can reuse an existing primitive

Suppose the durable inventory contains:

| Name | File | Public API | Shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| AppHeaderBar | `components/appHeaderBar/AppHeaderBar.kt` | leading/center/trailing slots | three-slot header with optional divider |
| PrimaryActionButton | `components/primaryActionButton/PrimaryActionButton.kt` | text, enabled, onClick | full-width rounded brand action |

A later generated screen contains one inline three-slot Row and one full-width brand action. Catalog both as `reuse`, even though each occurs once in the new batch:

```kotlin
AppHeaderBar(
    leading = {
        Icon(
            painter = painterResource(R.drawable.back),
            contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.back),
        )
    },
    center = {
        Text(
            text = stringResource(R.string.profile),
            style = CustomTheme.typography.header,
            color = CustomTheme.colors.textPrimary,
        )
    },
    trailing = {
        Icon(
            painter = painterResource(R.drawable.notifications),
            contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.notifications),
        )
    },
)

PrimaryActionButton(
    text = stringResource(R.string.save_changes),
    onClick = onSave,
)
```

Add the new screen to each component's callers in `shared-components.md` and the durable inventory.

## Equivalent shapes

These source forms often represent the same primitive when their screenshots, tokens, and interactions match:

| Primitive | Compose forms | SwiftUI forms |
|---|---|---|
| Three-slot header | `Row` with `SpaceBetween`; weighted Spacers; centered overlay | `HStack` with Spacers; `ZStack` with centered content |
| Primary action | `Button`; clickable `Surface`; clickable styled container | `Button`; project `ButtonStyle`; styled tappable container |
| Labeled input | `OutlinedTextField`; label + `BasicTextField`; decorated Row with icon slots | label + `TextField`; project `TextFieldStyle`; decorated HStack with `Image` slots |
| Segmented selector | `FilterChip` Row; segmented buttons; styled single-choice tabs | segmented `Picker`; typed Button Row |

Treat label text, selected values, icon content, and optional slot content as parameters. Preserve separate components when the widget, interaction, accessibility contract, or rendered structure differs. An unlabeled search prompt may therefore remain a distinct `SearchField` even when it shares tokens with a labeled form field.

## Generalization order

1. Reuse the current API when it already expresses the incoming case.
2. Add one typed optional value for a small variation.
3. Use view slots when callers supply different child view kinds.
4. Keep separate components when a shared API would hide meaningful behavioral differences.

Keep the existing canonical file, behavior, and callers source-compatible while applying the chosen change.
